name: boundry-verify
description: A local, read-only MCP server over sealed Boundry records. Contacts nothing; reads folders you declare. Requires Python 3.12 or newer.
long_description:
Requires Python 3.12 or newer. A stock macOS `python3` is older than that, and this package refuses before doing any work rather than running with parts of itself missing.

What it claims, in one sentence: one key signs everything and you hold it; the determinism shown is for the governed road, on the workloads in the kit, across the platforms named.

Nothing leaves your machine through this connector: it opens no socket and contacts no endpoint. Everything it renders is read by a model, as ordinary conversation content — see `PRIVACY.md`, which ships beside this file.

roots.title: Folders the connector may read
roots.description: Leave EMPTY to read only the packaged synthetic evaluation kit (`kit`) and demonstration records (`demo`), and nothing else. Otherwise a path-separator-delimited list, each entry a bare path or `label=path`; a folder you declare REPLACES the packaged ones. Name the folders you mean; do not give it a whole home directory.

tools.name: verify_record
tools.description: Check one sealed record with Boundry's INDEPENDENT verifier and report one of four outcomes: ATTESTED, REFUTED, ALTERED, UNATTESTED. UNATTESTED states a gap in the reader and is never a finding against the record. tenant_scope is REQUIRED — omitting it refuses rather than verifying any record in the directory. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: get_envelope
tools.description: Read one envelope. tenant_scope is REQUIRED — omitting it refuses rather than returning everything. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: query_envelopes
tools.description: List envelopes within a declared scope. tenant_scope is REQUIRED — absence of identity is not omniscience. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: chain_status
tools.description: Report what this reader can see of an artefact directory, each figure naming the instrument that produced it, and each figure it could NOT take named as not taken. tenant_scope is REQUIRED. Under per_tenant every figure is a figure of the declared scope and the cross-tenant figures are absent, not emptied. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: explain_record
tools.description: Render one record's provenance from the artefacts read during the call. Nothing is recalled from memory. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: check_plan_identity
tools.description: Recompute a sealed plan's id from its six inputs and check its seal, from a kernel export in a declared root. The id identifies the six inputs; the plan body is identified by the seal's content_hash. tenant_scope is REQUIRED. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.

tools.name: compare_runs
tools.description: Check two kernel exports against their own records, then compare them field by field and name each difference: EQUIVALENT, DIVERGENT or UNREACHABLE. This is hash comparison, not re-execution. tenant_scope is REQUIRED. A tool answers only inside the declared scope.
